literal: Of what use will a life excellent in its ways and great wealth become, if worthy ones of excellent virtue become angry?
translation: Of what avail are a life of excellent means and vast wealth, if worthy people of great virtue are provoked to anger?
modern: தகைமை சிறந்த தகுதியுடைய பெரியோர்கள் கோபித்துக் கொண்டால், எல்லா வழிகளிலும் சிறப்புற்ற வாழ்க்கையும், மிகப்பெரிய செல்வமும் இருந்தும் என்ன பயன் தரும்?
explanation: This couplet warns against incurring the wrath of great and worthy people. The word 'takkār' refers to those who are worthy and fit, possessing great virtue ('takai māṇṭa'). If such noble persons are provoked to anger ('ceṟiṉ'), then all the excellent ways of one's life ('vakaimāṇṭa vāḻkkai') and all one's vast wealth ('vāṉporuḷ') will become completely useless ('eṉṉām'). The repetition of 'māṇṭa' (excellent) emphasizes that even the most excellent worldly achievements and possessions cannot save a person from the ruin caused by offending the truly great.
